chapters.title: No Greater Joy Than Truth
chapters.synopsis: John writes to his wellbeloved Gaius, wishing that he may prosper and be in health even as his soul prospers, for John has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth. He commends Gaius for faithfully receiving the traveling brethren, rebukes Diotrephes, who loves preeminence and casts the faithful out of the church, and bears good witness of Demetrius. Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good.

segments.speaker: john-beloved
segments.note: Walk in truth; receive the faithful; follow good
